title: Native American Greenway at Lister Park
summary: A public marker beside the Mill River introduces Native histories of fishing, seasonal movement, and colonial displacement in the Rockville Centre landscape.
address_label: Lister Park, Riverside Road entrance, Rockville Centre
ancestral_territory_note: Merikoke and neighboring communities are remembered along the Mill River.
why_this_matters: A familiar riverside park can also be a place to learn whose histories shaped the landscape. The sign provides a concrete starting point for reading the Mill River alongside Native communities and colonial displacement.
introduction_title: Native History Beside the Mill River
introduction_content:
The Native American Greenway marker stands near the Riverside Road entrance to Lister Park, on the Mill River Green Way Trail. Its account names Merikoke, Rockaway, Canarsie, and Massapequa people in the river basin.1

Reading the Greenway Panel

The panel describes seasonal homes, tidal fish traps, gathered foods, hunting, and the making of tools and pottery. Its closing passage turns to colonial land transfers and displacement:1

“The tribes were driven to remote islands and marshes in Rockaway Bay and their lives were changed forever.”1

See Ian Lefkowitz’s October 4, 2025 photograph and the full inscription at the Historical Marker Database.1
history_content:
The marker describes fish traps, seasonal movement, and food gathering in the Mill River landscape. It also recounts the displacement of Native communities during colonial settlement.1

Its account names Merikoke, Rockaway, Canarsie, and Massapequa people, connecting the river with a wider network of neighboring communities.1

The river before the park

The panel’s account of fish traps and seasonal movement describes a river used through knowledge of its tides and surrounding habitats. Its named communities connect the Mill River with a wider South Shore world. Food gathering, toolmaking, and travel formed parts of the same landscape.1

The panel ends with colonial displacement. The story continues beyond that ending: the 1675 land complaint records Native resistance to colonial claims, and Montaukett outreach at Hempstead Lake brings present-day Native teaching into another part of this watershed. Nearby, the Culluloo Telewana Monument offers a contrasting example of how public memorials have represented Native people.23
whereintheworld_content: Find the sign near the Riverside Road entrance to Lister Park, along the Mill River Green Way Trail.1
